rows.sentence: Here are the steps from `doc.txt` as executable bullet points:
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This introduction announces the format of the answer rather than making a claim about the document's content.

rows.sentence: Start on the Adventure Screen.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document identifies the Adventure Screen as the starting screen.

rows.sentence: "What you will see first is the Adventure Screen." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The quotation directly matches the document.

rows.sentence: The world map is in the upper-right corner, and unexplored areas are black: "until you send a hero to explore an area you won't know what is there" (doc.txt).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives the map's location and explains that the black areas have not been explored.

rows.sentence: Confirm your hero is selected.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document identifies Lord Haart as the hero who should already be selected before you give instructions.

rows.sentence: "Your first hero, Lord Haart, should already be selected" (doc.txt).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly says Lord Haart should already be selected.

rows.sentence: Aim at the town entrance.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document directs the player to place the cursor over the town entrance.

rows.sentence: "place your mouse cursor over the entrance to the town (between the two flag poles)" (doc.txt); the horse icon rearing up means the hero will interact with that location.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document specifies where to place the cursor and explains what the rearing horse icon means.

rows.sentence: Click the location to set the path.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says the first click selects the path.

rows.sentence: "a set of green arrows show the path your hero will take to reach the large green X" (doc.txt), and the X "marks your hero's destination" (doc.txt).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explains that the arrows show the route and the X marks the destination.

rows.sentence: Click the same location again (or double-click) to send the hero.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explains that the second click sends the hero and that double-clicking performs both clicks.

rows.sentence: "Click again on the same location and your hero will move to the castle" (doc.txt).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly says clicking the same location again moves the hero to the castle.

rows.sentence: Wait for the Town Screen.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says the screen changes automatically when the hero arrives at the town entrance.

rows.sentence: "When the hero arrives at the entrance to the town, the view will change to the Town Screen." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The quotation directly matches the document's description of the screen transition.

rows.sentence: Check the town info in the bottom-left corner, which shows "town income (per day) and troop production (per week)" (doc.txt); the top row of boxes is the garrison, the bottom row is troops visiting with a hero.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document confirms the location and contents of the town information and identifies what each row of boxes displays.

rows.sentence: Build a Fort: "click on the larger of the two buildings on the left side of the town view – the Town Hall – to enter the Hall Screen" (doc.txt).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this as the first step in building a Fort.

rows.sentence: Read the building color codes on the Hall Screen: "Any building you can currently build is shown with its name in a green bar" (doc.txt); "Any building that you can not build, but can be built later is shown with its name in a red bar" (doc.txt); "If a building has been disabled or can never be built, its name will appear in a gray bar" (doc.txt); "Once you have completely built or upgraded a structure as high as it will go, its name will be displayed in gold" (doc.txt).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly gives all four color codes and their meanings.

rows.sentence: Build the Fort: "Click on the picture of the Fort" (doc.txt) to see its description and required resources, then "Click on the Build button (in the lower left hand corner of the popup window) and the Fort will be constructed." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document confirms what clicking the Fort picture displays and where to click to build it.

rows.sentence: Inspect the Castle Window: "click on it to view the Castle Window" (doc.txt), which "shows you information about all seven units that can be produced by this town" (doc.txt); built Creature Generators (currently the Guardhouse, Archers' Tower, and Barracks) show units available.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says clicking the Fort opens the Castle Window, describes its seven-unit overview, and names the three structures with units available.

rows.sentence: Click Exit (lower right) to return to the Town Screen.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives both the location of the Exit button and the screen it returns you to.

rows.sentence: Buy a spell book at the Mage Guild (the round tower on the right): "All heroes must have a spell book before they can learn or cast spells." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document identifies the Mage Guild, directs the player to buy a spell book there, and explains why one is required.

rows.sentence: Browse spells on the Mage Guild Screen: "Left or right clicking on any spell scroll will show you a description of that spell." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says the spells appear on scrolls in the Mage Guild and either kind of click opens a description.

rows.sentence: Click Exit (lower right) to leave.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this exact way to leave the Mage Guild.

rows.sentence: Recruit troops: "Click on the large central tower.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document directs the player to click the large central tower to start recruiting Pikemen.

rows.sentence: The Recruit Pikemen window is displayed." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly names the window that appears.

rows.sentence: Choose the quantity: use the scroll bar to select a number (total cost is calculated to the right), or "the fastest way to buy troops is to use the Maximum button (the four up arrows at the bottom of the popup window)" (doc.txt), which buys the maximum you can afford.
rows.label: contradictory
rows.rationale: The scroll bar and button details are correct, but Maximum only calculates the affordable quantity; the separate Recruit button completes the purchase.

rows.sentence: Confirm the purchase: "Click the Maximum button, then click the Recruit button (bottom center).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this button sequence and identifies the position of the Recruit button.

rows.sentence: Notice how there are now Pikemen in the garrison row of your town." (doc.txt)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly says the recruited Pikemen appear in the town's garrison row.
